The claim for compensation in the present claim petition relates to injuries and disability suffered by petitioner in a road accident that took place on 31.07.2016, at about 3.30 pm, Near Village Dewla Petrol Pump, Gautam Budh Nagar, U.P., regarding which an FIR bearing no.563/2016, under Sections 279/338/304-A IPC was registered at PS Surajpur, U.P.

The case of petitioner, briefly stated, is that on the aforesaid date, time and place of accident, the petitioner was sitting as a pillion rider on a motorcycle bearing registration No. UP-16BA-5626,
which was being driven by Sh. Ajay Singh and they were proceeding towards Bulandshahar from Noida.

When they reached near Village Dewla Petrol Pump, the offending vehicle bearing registration No. DL-AGB-7981, which was being driven by respondent no. 1 in rash and negligent manner, came from behind and hit their motorcycle due to which the petitioner Subodh sustained grievous injuries and Sh. Ajay Singh sustained fatal injuries.
It is further stated that the petitioner was taken to Max Hospital and thereafter shifted to Safdarjung Hospital for further treatment.

3. Respondent no. 1 has filed his written statement wherein it is stated that the alleged accident was not caused by the vehicle bearing registration No. DL-AGB-7981 and he was driving the vehicle as per traffic norms.
It is further stated that the petitioner is not entitled to any compensation as the accident took place due to negligence of petitioner himself.

4. It is pertinent to mention here that R-2 had not appeared before the tribunal despite service by way of publication in the newspaper "Veer Arjun" and hence, the respondent no. 2 was proceeded ex-parte vide order dated 27.08.2018.
5.
Respondent no. 3/Insurance Company had filed written statement wherein it is stated that there is an unexplained delay of 12 days in the registration of FIR in respect of alleged accident.
It is further stated that there is no MLC of the injured to show that he sustained alleged injuries on the alleged date of accident.
It is further stated that there is no whisper as to how the vehicle described as the offending vehicle is being connected to the alleged accident.

6. On 27.08.2018, the following issues were framed by the Ld. Predecessor of this tribunal as :-
1.

Whether the injured Subodh Kumar sustained injuries in the accident which occurred on 31.07.2016, at about 3.30 pm, Near Village Dewla Petrol Pump, PS Surajpur, Gautam Budh Nagar, U.P. caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle No. DL-AGB-7981 being driven by respondent no. 1, owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with respondent no. 3 ? OPP.

The case record has also been perused, including the written submissions filed on behalf of petitioner.

During cross-examination, PW1 deposed that the motorcycle was being driven by Sh. Ajad Singh at the relevant time of accident.
He denied the suggestion that the accident took place due to negligence of Sh. Azad and also denied that there were three riders on the motorcycle at the time of accident.
He further deposed that he does not know whether Sh. Azad was having valid driving license to drive motorcycle or not.

No other witness was examined on behalf of petitioner and no evidence was led by respondent no. 3.
9.

During the course of final arguments, Ld. Counsel for Insurance Company has argued that there is unexplained delay of about 12 days in registration of FIR as the accident took place on 31.07.2016 and the FIR got registered on 12.08.2016.

On this point, reliance has been placed upon the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case Ravi Vs. Badrinarayan, Civil Appeal No. 1926 of 2011 (arising out of S.L.P. (C) No.11974 of 2008),
decided on 18.02.2011 wherein it was held :-
"......21.

sentences.text: The purpose of lodging the FIR in such type of cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences.
Lodging of FIR certainly proves factum of accident so that the victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.

In other words, although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases,
delay in lodging the same should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
Unless kith and kin of the victim are able to regain a certain level of tranquility of mind and are composed to lodge it, even if, there is delay, the same deserves to be condoned.
In such circumstances, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof supported by cogent reasons."
In view of the aforesaid judgment, the delay in filing of FIR cannot be a ground for dismissal of claim petition.
10. Further, Ld. Counsel for Insurance Company has argued that there were three persons on the bike at the time of accident which is against the traffic rules.

However, during cross examination,
PW1 denied the suggestion that there were three persons on the motorcycle at the time of accident.

such as FIR, recovery memo and mechanical inspection report of vehicle are documents of sufficient proof to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent and the proceedings under Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to proceedings in a civil suit and hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard."

Further, it is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters, the facts are required to be established on preponderance of probabilities and not beyond reasonable doubt, as are required in a criminal prosecution.

Reference in this regard is made to the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court reported as (2009) 13 SC 530 in Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein it has been observed :-
"......Strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants and the claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability."

ISSUE NO.2 Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?

13 . As the issue no.1 has been proved in favour of the petitioner, he has become entitled to be compensated for the injuries suffered by him in the accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.

In terms of provisions contained in Section 168 of the MV Act the compensation which is to be awarded by this tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In injury cases, a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensation i.e. pecuniary as well as non-pecuniary damages.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in case titled as Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar (2011) 1 SCC 343) has laid down heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases:-
Pecuniary damages (Special Damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising :
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment;
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.

Non-pecuniary damages (General Damages)
(iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage).

(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).

Having considered the ratio of aforesaid judgment, the compensation payable to petitioner is assessed hereinafter under the following heads:-
(I) Medical or Treatment Expenses 16.

The petitioner in his affidavit Ex. PW1/A has tendered on record discharge summary as Ex.
PW1/3 and medical treatment record as Ex. PW1/4 which reflects that the petitioner was initially taken to government hospital at Bulandshahar, U.P. and thereafter shifted to Safdarjung Hospital,
New Delhi where he was admitted on 01.08.2016 and was discharged on 07.09.2016.

It further reflects that the petitioner had suffered degloving injury in right leg extending from 5 cm lower to patella to right heel with no bone injury and had also undergone debridement and SSG was done under SA.
Petitioner has also tendered on record his medical bills as Ex. PW1/5 (colly) which are totalling to a sum of Rs. 3,049/-.
Needless to say, the insurance company has not led any evidence to show that the said bills do not relate to the injuries suffered by the petitioner in the aforesaid accident.

Thus,

In the absence of any plausible evidence produced by respondents on record, there is no reason to disbelieve the testimony of PW-1 that he has spent the aforesaid amount towards medical expenses.
Hence, he is held entitled to Rs. 3,049/- towards his medical expenses.
(II) Loss of actual earnings 17.
The petitioner in his affidavit Ex. PW1/A has claimed that he was working as a helper with New Ashok Nagar DJ at Delhi and was earning about Rs. 12,000/- per month.

During cross examination,
he deposed that he was employed at Delhi and was also sent to Noida for his work as DJ Operator.
But he admitted that he has not filed any document to substantiate that he was working as a helper at Delhi.

Since the profession and income of the petitioner has not been proved on record, the minimum wages of unskilled worker is taken into account as per rates prevalent in U.P., which was Rs. 7,108/-
(rounded off) per month at the time of accident.
Keeping in view the duration of his treatment, this tribunal feels it just and reasonable to compensate him for loss of earning equivalent to a period of 4 months.
Therefore, under this head, he is being awarded an amount of Rs. 28,432/- (Rs. 7,108/- X 4 months).
(III) Loss of future earnings due to disability 18.

As per disability certificate dated 23.12.2019 as Ex. PW1/7, the petitioner is a case of RTA with injury to right ankle and foot (heel pad avulsion) and his permanent physical disability is 20% in relation to right lower limb.

19. The law with regard to grant of compensation due to permanent disability and determination of functional disability etc. was well settled by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Raj Kumar Vs.
Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343, wherein it has been held as under :-
"10.

sentences.text: Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps.

The Tribunal has to first ascertain what activities the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of the permanent ability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident, as also his age.

The third step is to find out whether (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any kind of livelihood, or (ii) whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (iii) whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions, but could carry on some other or lesser scale of activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood.

For example, if the left hand of a claimant is amputated, the permanent Subodh Kumar vs . Sanjay Kumar & on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56614926/
6 physical or functional disablement may be assessed around 60%.
If the claimant was a driver or a carpenter, the actual loss of earning capacity may virtually be hundred percent, if he is neither able to drive or do carpentry.

On the other hand, if the claimant was a clerk in government service, the loss of his left hand may not result in loss of employment and he may still be continued as a clerk as he could perform his clerical functions; and in that event the loss of earning capacity will not be 100% as in the case of a driver or carpenter, nor 60% which is the actual physical disability, but far less.

In fact, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of `loss of future earnings', if the claimant continues in government service,
though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities as a consequence of losing his hand.

Sometimes the injured claimant may be continued in service, but may not found suitable for discharging the duties attached to the post or job which he was earlier holding, on account of his disability, and may therefore be shifted to some other suitable but lesser post with lesser emoluments, in which case there should be a limited award under the head of loss of future earning capacity,
taking note of the reduced earning capacity.

It may be noted that when compensation is awarded by treating the loss of future earning capacity as 100% (or even anything more than 50%), the need to award compensation separately under the head of loss of amenities or loss of expectation of life may disappear and as a result, only a token or nominal amount may have to be awarded under the head of loss of amenities or loss of expectation of life, as otherwise there may be a duplication in the award of compensation.
Be that as it may.

20. Keeping in view the ratio of aforesaid case and the nature of disability suffered by the petitioner as well as considering his job/profession, the functional disability of the petitioner is taken as 10% in relation to whole body, i.e. half of the disability mentioned in the disability certificate.
21. Further, to apply the multiplier, it is necessary to ascertain the age of the petitioner.
The petitioner has tendered on record copy of his Aadhar card as Ex. PW1/1 in which his date of birth is mentioned as 01.01.1995.
Hence, going by these documents, his age as on 31.07.2016 i.e. date of accident was 21 years, 6 months and 30 days.

Therefore, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr., (2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Apex Court in a judgment of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. SLP (Civil) No. 25590 of 2014 decided on 31.10.2017, the multiplier of 18 is applicable for calculating the loss of future earnings of the petitioner arising out of above disability.

As stated above, the petitioner had suffered grievous injuries in the accident.

However, it is not possible to exactly compensate him for the shock, pain and sufferings etc. which he had actually suffered because of the above injuries and disability, but an effort has to be made to compensate him for the same in a just and reasonable manner.

Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of Rs.40,000/- each is being awarded to him towards mental and physical shock & for pain and sufferings.
Further, an amount of Rs.20,000/- is also awarded to him towards the loss of amenities suffered by him during the said period of his treatment.
Thus, he is awarded total amount of Rs.1,00,000/- under this head.
(V) Conveyance, Special Diet and Attendant Charges 23.

The petitioner in his affidavit Ex. PW1/A has claimed that he had spent an amount of Rs.
60,000/- towards special diet and attendant.
Further, he has tendered on record the ambulance bills as Ex. PW1/6 for visiting hospital from his native place.

the insurance company has not led any evidence to show that the said ambulance bills are forged and fabricated.
Perusal of record reveals that the ambulance bills Ex. PW1/6 are totalling to a sum of Rs. 33,000/-.
However, the petitioner has not placed on record any documentary evidence to substantiate his above claim regarding amount spent towards special diet.
Still this tribunal can very well take note of the requirement of special diet for early recovery of petitioner from the injuries suffered because of the accident.
Hence, an amount of Rs.20,000/- is being awarded to the petitioner towards special diet and the above amount of Rs. 33,000/- is being awarded to the petitioner towards conveyance.

Besides the above, an amount of Rs.6,000/ per month for 4 months is also being granted to him towards attendant charges or for the gratuitous services rendered by his family members during the period of hospitalization and immobility.

Therefore, a total amount of Rs. 77,000/ (Rs. 20,000/ +
Rs. 33,000/ + Rs. 24,000/) is being awarded to him under this head.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In view of the aforesaid judgment, the delay in filing of FIR cannot be a ground for dismissal of claim petition.
Further, it is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters, the facts are required to be established on preponderance of probabilities and not beyond reasonable doubt, as are required in a criminal prosecution.
In view of foregoing discussion, this issue is duly substantiated by ocular evidence of injured as PW1 and the documentary evidence in form of chargesheet etc.
and thus, it stands proved on preponderance of probabilities that the aforesaid accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing no. DL-AGB-7981 which was being driven by respondent no.
1, owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with respondent no. 3 at the relevant time of accident.
Hence, this issue is decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.
In terms of provisions contained in Section 168 of the MV Act the compensation which is to be awarded by this tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In injury cases, a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensation i.e. pecuniary as well as non-pecuniary damages.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in case titled as Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar (2011) 1 SCC 343) has laid down heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases:-
Pecuniary damages (Special Damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising :
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment;
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.
Thus,

"10.
The Tribunal has to first ascertain what activities the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of the permanent ability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident, as also his age.
On the other hand, if the claimant was a clerk in government service, the loss of his left hand may not result in loss of employment and he may still be continued as a clerk as he could perform his clerical functions; and in that event the loss of earning capacity will not be 100% as in the case of a driver or carpenter, nor 60% which is the actual physical disability, but far less.
In fact, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of `loss of future earnings', if the claimant continues in government service,
though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities as a consequence of losing his hand.
Therefore, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr., (2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Apex Court in a judgment of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. SLP (Civil) No. 25590 of 2014 decided on 31.10.2017, the multiplier of 18 is applicable for calculating the loss of future earnings of the petitioner arising out of above disability.
